function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

Click “Go” and wait for the results. | | **Command line (Windows)** | If you have the Speedtest CLI installed, open PowerShell or Command Prompt and type:
`speedtest`
It will report download, upload, and ping. | | **Command line (Linux/macOS)** | Install the CLI (`sudo apt install speedtest-cli` or `brew install speedtest-cli`) and run `speedtest`. | | **Mobile app** | Download the official Speedtest app from Google Play or the App Store and run a test. | If you want to automate it from a script, you can use the `speedtest-cli` package. For example, in Python: ```python import speedtest s = speedtest.Speedtest() s.get_best_server() download = s.download() / 1_000_000 # Mbps upload = s.upload() / 1_000_000 # Mbps print(f"Download: {download:.2f} Mbps, Upload: {upload:.2f} Mbps") ``` Just run that on your machine and you’ll get the current speeds. Let me know if you need help installing or running any of these tools!
